simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to דָּגָה (H1710) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-f.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 15 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: דָּגָה (dâgâh) means fish. First listed occurrence: Deut 4 18.

definitions.full: H1710. dagah דָּגָה noun feminine fish (Late Hebrew id. ) — דָּגָה Num 11:5 5 t.; construct דְּגַת Gen 1:26 4 t. + Ezek 29:4 b (strike out B Co); suffix דְּגָתוֺ 47:10 ᵑ9 ᵐ5 Co; ( דגתם ᵑ0 ), דְּגָתָם Isa 50:2 ; Psa 105:29 + Ezek 47:10 ᵑ0 compare above — fish , almost always collective; fish of sea הַיָּם דְּגַת Gen 1:26 , 28 (P) Ezek 47:10 (in simile); in Nile ( יְאֹר ) Exod 7:18 , 21 (E) compare Psa 105:29 , יְאֹרֶיךָ דְּגַת Ezek 29:4 (twice in verse) (compare above) 29:5 ; in sea and rivers Isa 50:2 ; Ezek 47:9-10 , food in Egypt Num 11:5 (JE); image of fish forbidden in worship, as of beasts and birds Deut 4:18 (on sacredness of fish, and use in sacrifice compare Selden De Diis Syris, ii. 3. RS Sern. i. 274 ); of single fish only Jonah 2:2 ( 2:1 (twice in verse); Jonah 2:11 דָּג ) by late usage; compare conversely דָּאג = דָּגָה collective Neh 13:16 .
definitions.rootNote: feminine of 1709 , and meaning the same
